rv.q: It nonetheless comes with an enormous gut-punch, and is all that theatre should strive to be.
Omran’s firebrand lead performance is something to behold.

Sami Ibrahim's unrestrained and unwieldy script is cluttered with compelling yet underdeveloped threads, ghostly metaphors, and awkward jokes clustered around a familiar story about the futility of violence.
As it is, ‘Two Palestinians Go Dogging’ feels like a lengthy brainstorming session on how to write a great original play about Palestine, rather than a great original play about Palestine.
The show is a mess and a bore but it has also lodged in my brain like a nagging earworm.
The overall whole hangs together surprisingly well.
This play may be a metaphor but, when not being shouted at, its bleak picture of the current situation continuing into the future, perhaps getting even worse, can be very moving.
This crazy sci-fi twist makes everything daft and weightless.
I reflect on an entertaining evening that tackled difficult subject matter with deft humour and inventive staging.

cn.t: Ibrahim's audacious dark comedy about the Israeli-Palestinian conflict divides critics with its irreverent approach and Brechtian techniques—some praise its originality and power, while others find it unfocused, annoying, or overly confrontational.
